rules: Short sentences. No jargon. Never diagnose. Always say when to tell the crew medical officer (CMO). Reviewed by the team; to be reviewed by flight medicine experts.

isolation.name: Isolation and confinement
isolation.text: Small spaces, the same few faces and no real sunrise wear down sleep and mood over months.

gravity.name: Gravity fields
gravity.text: Low gravity shifts body fluids toward the head and changes how the heart and blood vessels work.

closed.name: Hostile closed environment
closed.text: Recycled air, shared surfaces and a busy schedule make infections and stress easier to pick up.

distance.name: Distance from Earth
distance.text: Help from Earth takes many minutes each way, so the crew must act first and report after.

radiation.name: Space radiation
radiation.text: Radiation outside Earth's magnetic field slowly affects blood, immunity and long-term health.

brain-green.title: Sleep and mood look like you.
brain-green.what: Your sleep and mood are inside your normal.
do_now: Get some light and movement early in the day.
brain-green.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if you feel low for several days, even if the numbers look fine.
brain-green.why_this_check: Sleep and mood change first when a long mission starts to wear you down.
brain-green.source: NASA HRP hazards: isolation and confinement

sleep-yellow.title: You are short on sleep.
sleep-yellow.what: You slept less than you need, or less than your normal.
do_now: Dim the lights an hour before bed.
sleep-yellow.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if you are still short on sleep at the recheck, or after three nights.
sleep-yellow.why_this_check: Short sleep slows reactions and changes mood within days. On a mission that affects safety.
sleep-yellow.source: NASA HRP hazards; AASM/SRS adult sleep consensus (terrestrial); NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 6001]

sleep-red.title: Very little sleep two nights running.
sleep-red.what: Under 4 hours of sleep two nights in a row.
do_now: Do not do hazardous tasks or an EVA until you have rested.
Plan a protected sleep period today.
sleep-red.why_this_check: Severe sleep loss makes mistakes much more likely.

mood-yellow.title: Your mood is lower than usual.
mood-yellow.what: Your mood is below your normal, or low for a few days.
do_now: Talk to a crewmate you trust today.
Take a short break from screens.
Do something you enjoy, even for 10 minutes.
mood-yellow.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if this lasts three days, or right away if you feel very low.
mood-yellow.why_this_check: Long isolation lowers mood slowly. Noticing it early makes it easier to fix.
mood-yellow.source: NASA HRP hazards: isolation and confinement; project-defined

heart-green.title: Heart rate and blood pressure look like you.
heart-green.what: Both are inside the usual range and your normal.
heart-green.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if you feel dizzy, faint or have chest pain at any time.
heart-green.why_this_check: Low gravity changes how the heart works. Your own trend shows it first.

hr-yellow.title: Your resting heart rate is off your normal.
hr-yellow.what: Your resting heart rate is outside your normal or the usual range.
do_now: Sit still for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note caffeine, exercise or stress in the last hour.
hr-yellow.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it is still off at the recheck, or if you feel dizzy or short of breath.
hr-yellow.why_this_check: A resting heart rate that drifts up can be an early sign of poor sleep, stress, dehydration or illness.

hr-red.title: Your heart rate needs help now.
hr-red.what: Your resting heart rate is far outside the safe range.
do_now: Stop what you are doing and sit or lie down.
Measure again in 2 minutes while you wait.
Do not do an EVA or hazardous task.
hr-red.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
hr-red.why_this_check: A very slow or very fast resting heart rate can be serious.

bp-yellow.title: Your blood pressure is higher than usual.
bp-yellow.what: Your blood pressure is above the usual range or your normal.
do_now: Sit quietly for 5 minutes, feet flat, arm at heart level, and measure again.
Cut down on salty food today.
bp-yellow.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it is still high at the recheck, or if you have a headache or blurred vision.
bp-yellow.why_this_check: Fluid shifts in low gravity change blood pressure. Catching a change early is easy to act on.

bp-red.title: Your blood pressure needs help now.
bp-red.what: Your blood pressure is at a crisis level.
do_now: Tell the CMO about any chest pain, headache, weakness or trouble seeing.
bp-red.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
bp-red.why_this_check: Very high blood pressure can harm the heart, brain and kidneys.

blood-green.title: Blood sugar looks like you.
blood-green.what: Your blood sugar is inside the usual range and your normal.
blood-green.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if you feel shaky, sweaty or confused at any time.
blood-green.why_this_check: Diet, stress and low activity in space can change how the body handles sugar.
blood-green.source: ADA Standards of Care, fasting glucose (terrestrial)

glucose-yellow-high.title: Your blood sugar is a bit high.
glucose-yellow-high.what: Your fasting blood sugar is above the usual range or your normal.
do_now: Make sure this was a fasting reading (no food for 8 hours).
Check again tomorrow morning before eating.
glucose-yellow-high.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it is high again tomorrow.
glucose-yellow-high.why_this_check: A single high reading is common. A pattern is worth knowing about early.
glucose-yellow-high.source: ADA Standards of Care, fasting glucose (terrestrial)

glucose-yellow-low.title: Your blood sugar is a bit low.
glucose-yellow-low.what: Your blood sugar is below the usual range.
do_now: Eat or drink something with sugar now (juice or a sweet).
glucose-yellow-low.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it is still low after 15 minutes, or if you feel shaky or confused.
glucose-yellow-low.why_this_check: Low blood sugar can make you shaky, slow and confused.
glucose-yellow-low.source: ADA Standards of Care, level 1 hypoglycaemia (terrestrial)

glucose-red-low.title: Your blood sugar is too low.
glucose-red-low.what: Your blood sugar is under 54 mg/dL.
do_now: Eat or drink 15 g of fast sugar now (juice or glucose tablets).
Sit down. Do not do hazardous tasks.
glucose-red-low.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
glucose-red-low.why_this_check: Very low blood sugar can cause confusion or fainting quickly.
glucose-red-low.source: ADA Standards of Care, level 2 hypoglycaemia (terrestrial)

glucose-red-high.title: Your blood sugar is very high.
glucose-red-high.what: Your blood sugar is 250 mg/dL or more.
glucose-red-high.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
glucose-red-high.why_this_check: Very high blood sugar needs medical attention.

skin-green.title: Temperature looks like you.
skin-green.what: Your temperature is inside the usual range and your normal.
do_now: Wash hands before meals and after the toilet.
skin-green.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if you feel feverish or unwell.
skin-green.why_this_check: In a closed habitat, infections spread easily. Temperature is the quickest early sign.
skin-green.source: NASA HRP hazards: hostile closed environment

temp-yellow-high.title: You have a raised temperature.
temp-yellow-high.what: Your temperature is above the usual range.
do_now: Wear a mask in shared areas and clean surfaces you touch.
temp-yellow-high.escalate_if: Tell the CMO today. Tell them right away if it goes over 39.5 °C or you feel worse.
temp-yellow-high.why_this_check: A fever in a closed habitat can spread to the whole crew.

temp-yellow-low.title: Your temperature is a bit low.
temp-yellow-low.what: Your temperature is below the usual range.
do_now: Measure again with the thermometer in the right place.
Put on warm layers and have a warm drink.
temp-yellow-low.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it stays low or you feel very cold or confused.
temp-yellow-low.why_this_check: A low reading is often a measuring error, but a real one needs warming up.

temp-red-high.title: You have a high fever.
do_now: Rest, drink water, and keep away from crewmates.
temp-red-high.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
temp-red-high.why_this_check: A high fever needs medical care, and may spread to the crew.

temp-red-low.title: Your temperature is too low.
do_now: Warm up slowly: dry clothes, blankets, warm drink.
temp-red-low.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
temp-red-low.why_this_check: A very low body temperature needs care right away.

pattern-fatigue.title: Fatigue pattern
pattern-fatigue.what: Short sleep, a raised resting heart rate and a lower mood, all on the same day. Together they point to one thing: you are running down.
do_now: Protect tonight's sleep: same bedtime, lights dim an hour before.
Ask to move one demanding task if you can.
pattern-fatigue.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it is still yellow at the recheck.
pattern-fatigue.why_this_check: Each sign alone is small. Together they are an early warning worth one simple plan.

pattern-fever.title: Possible infection
pattern-fever.what: A raised temperature and a raised heart rate together.
do_now: Wear a mask in shared areas.
pattern-fever.escalate_if: Tell the CMO today. Tell them right away if you feel worse.
pattern-fever.why_this_check: In a closed habitat, an infection is a crew problem, not just yours.

pattern-ortho.title: Light-headed when you stand up
pattern-ortho.what: You feel dizzy on standing and your blood pressure is low for you.
do_now: Sit or lie down now, legs raised.
Drink 500 mL of water or an electrolyte drink.
Stand up slowly, in two steps.
Tell the CMO today and measure again lying, then standing.
pattern-ortho.escalate_if: Call the CMO now if you faint, have chest pain, or it does not ease when you lie down.
pattern-ortho.why_this_check: After a change in gravity, the body can be slow to keep blood pressure up when standing. Most astronauts feel this after landing.
pattern-ortho.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C Table E.2-2 (gravity-transition orthostatic intolerance); project-defined trigger

crt-yellow.title: Your fingertip is slow to pink up.
crt-yellow.what: Capillary refill is slower than the usual range, or slower than your normal.
do_now: Warm your hands for a minute, cold hands slow this test.
crt-yellow.escalate_if: Tell the CMO if it is still slow at the recheck, or if you also feel dizzy or faint.
crt-yellow.why_this_check: Fluid shifts in low gravity change blood pressure and circulation. A slow fingertip refill is an early, physical sign worth a second look.
crt-yellow.source: Experimental camera-based self-test; team-defined, not clinically validated

crt-red.title: Your capillary refill needs help now.
crt-red.what: Capillary refill of 4.5 seconds or more.
do_now: Mention any dizziness, faintness or cold, pale hands.
Retest in a few minutes while you wait.
crt-red.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
crt-red.why_this_check: A very slow return of colour to the fingertip can point to poor circulation or significant fluid loss.
crt-red.source: Project-defined red limit; experimental camera-based self-test, not clinically validated

symptoms-red.title: Act now
symptoms-red.what: You reported a warning sign that always needs help right away.
do_now: Stop what you are doing. Sit or lie down somewhere safe.
Call the CMO now. Say what you feel.
Do not be alone. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
symptoms-red.escalate_if: The CMO has been alerted. A summary is going to Earth.
symptoms-red.why_this_check: These warning signs can be serious. Earth is minutes away, so the crew acts first.
symptoms-red.source: Project-defined, based on standard emergency warning signs

measure.bp_sys: Sit for 5 minutes, back supported, feet flat. Cuff on bare upper arm at heart level. Don't talk. Take two readings 1 minute apart.
measure.bp_dia: Same reading as systolic: the lower number.
measure.hr: At rest, sitting, before coffee or exercise. Use the cuff or a chest strap, or count your pulse for 60 seconds.
measure.glucose: Fasting: before breakfast, at least 8 hours after food. Clean, dry finger. Use the second drop.
measure.temp: Thermometer under the tongue, mouth closed, for the full time. No hot or cold drinks for 15 minutes before.
measure.sleep: Hours of real sleep last night, not time in bed. Your watch or your best guess to the half hour.
measure.mood: How you feel overall right now. 1 = very low, 3 = okay, 5 = great. Be honest; nobody else sees it.
measure.crt: Optional camera check. Press a fingertip firmly over the camera lens for 5 seconds to blanch it, then move it just clear of the lens. ASCLEPIUS times how long the skin takes to pink up again. No camera, or prefer not to: use the manual stopwatch instead.
